mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for two consecutive months indicates an overheating labor market, which typically precedes either aggressive Fed tightening or wage inflation, both of which historically precede negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 shows two consecutive quarterly declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 200,000 in a single month, combined with a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a mismatch between job creation and labor force participation, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month +200000 AND UNRATE > previous month +0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) for four consecutive months, regardless of other macro conditions, is a leading indicator of weakening consumer demand and typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 6% month-over-month, accompanied by a federal funds rate that has not yet increased in the prior two months, signals a delayed monetary policy response that typically results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as markets anticipate easing.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > previous month +6% AND FEDFUNDS == previous month for 2 months
regime_hint: post-shock inflation with lagged policy response
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1%, coupled with a simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10,000 units, signals a broad-based supply expansion in both manufacturing and housing, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month +1% AND HOUST > previous month +10000
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.
